findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 Committee report template
findings.headline: Investment income fell by a third, reducing unrestricted revenue base
findings.detail: Interest earned decreased 32.97% to £1.503m in 2025/26, driven by both lower cash balances and falling Bank of England base rates (from 4.50% to 3.75%). The council's treasury strategy relies on investment returns to supplement revenue.
findings.matters: A significant drop in investment income reduces discretionary revenue available for services or capital funding and suggests the council will face tighter budget constraints in coming years.
findings.figures: Interest earned 2025/26: £1,503k; decrease of 32.97% on prior year; average yield 3.63%
findings.quote: Interest earned decreased by 32.97% compared to 2024/25, due to the reduced available cash balances to invest.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26 Committee report template
findings.headline: Cash available for investment fell sharply year-on-year despite no external borrowing need
findings.detail: Average daily investment balances declined from £44.498m to £37.103m, a drop of 16.62%. The council continued its strategy of self-financing capital expenditure using its own cash rather than external borrowing, but the cash base to support this is shrinking.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know if a council's liquid reserves are in structural decline, as this constrains financial flexibility, may eventually force external borrowing, and indicates tighter cash management.
findings.figures: Average daily investment 2025/26: £37.103m; 2024/25: £44.498m; reduction of £7.395m or 16.62%
findings.quote: The average daily balance of £37.103m shown above is 16.62% less than the 2024/25 figure of £44.498m.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation funding commitment of £720k over two years with £360k allocated in 2025-26
findings.detail: South Ribble is allocating £360k of 2025-26 underspend to a Local Government Reorganisation reserve. The council's total financial commitment to the Lancashire-wide reorganisation programme is £720,000 over two years, drawn from a total Lancashire reorganisation fund of £30m. This represents a material known future expenditure alongside any service restructuring.
findings.matters: Major local government reorganisation creates financial uncertainty and commits resources to implementation costs; affects medium-term financial forecasting and may lead to service changes
findings.figures: £360k allocated 2025-26; total South Ribble commitment £720k over two years; total Lancashire pot £30m
findings.quote: To allocate an initial £360k of this underspend towards a Local Government Reorganisation reserve to help fund the Lancashire wide programme. The total value currently required from South Ribble Council is £720,000 across two years from the total Lancashire pot of £30m.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Property portfolio rental and service charge income shortfall of £31k attributed to vacant units and office redesign impact
findings.detail: The Property directorate underachieved rental and service charge income by £31k. This reflects vacant units within investment properties and reduced income from community facilities and the Civic Centre during office and Council Chamber redesign work. The council anticipates improved income once a new bookings system is implemented.
findings.matters: Property portfolio income gaps suggest asset management challenges or market conditions affecting rental performance; vacant units represent underutilised assets
findings.figures: £31k under achieved rental and service charge income; attributed to vacant units and facility redesign period
findings.quote: £31k under achieved rental and service charge income across the directorate compared to budget. This is due to a combination of a few vacant units within the investment properties. This also includes the reduction in rental income for Moss Side Community Centre, the Civic Centre and the Conference Facilities, due to the in-year re-design of offices and Council Chamber

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Worden Hall venue income underperformed by £65k due to reduced room and wedding bookings
findings.detail: Worden Hall events overspent by £65k against its budgeted income for room and wedding bookings. The council reports ongoing promotion and development work on the facility, indicating it is operating below expected income capacity.
findings.matters: Council venue asset underperformance against income targets indicates either market conditions limiting bookings or management challenges in generating expected revenue
findings.figures: £65k net overspend on Worden Hall events
findings.quote: £65k net overspend on Worden Hall events mainly due to the reduced level of room and wedding bookings income compared to the budget. Work is on-going on the promotion and development of the Worden Hall.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Housing Benefit and Supported Housing costs overshot by £151k including £227k overspend on Supported Housing with increased subsidy loss claims of £117k
findings.detail: Within the Corporate budget, Housing Benefit costs exceeded budget by £151k. This includes a £227k overspend on Supported Housing specifically, and increased subsidy loss claims of £117k compared to 2024-25. The scale of the increase suggests growing housing support demand and subsidy requirements not anticipated in the budget.
findings.matters: Growing housing support costs and subsidy claims indicate demographic or economic pressure on housing need that may persist; subsidy changes also affect council funding stability
findings.figures: £151k net overspend on Housing Benefit; £227k on Supported Housing; subsidy loss claim increase of £117,166
findings.quote: £151k net overspend within Housing Benefit... This also includes net overspend of £227k relating to increased expenditure linked to Supported Housing, increase in subsidy loss claim (60% subsidy) of £117,166 and increase in nil subsidy of £26,040 compared to 2024/25 final claim.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: General Fund reserves drawn down by £833k in 2025-26 to £4.334m, now only £334k above the minimum threshold of £4.0m
findings.detail: Unearmarked reserves fell from £5.167m at 1 April 2025 to £4.334m at 31 March 2026. The council's Medium-Term Financial Strategy specifies a minimum reserve level of £4.0m, leaving a cushion of just £334k. This is materially tighter than the previous year and represents limited buffer for unexpected costs.
findings.matters: Reserve adequacy directly affects council resilience to handle spending pressures or income shortfalls; minimum reserves at £4.0m limits financial flexibility
findings.figures: General Fund 1 April 2025: £5.167m; 31 March 2026: £4.334m; Minimum threshold £4.0m; 2025-26 drawdown £833k
findings.quote: As at 1 April 2025 the Council held a (£5.167m) General Fund Reserve... the closing balance on the General Fund Reserve will be (£4.334m)... the minimum level of General Fund Reserves should be maintained at (£4.0m)

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Trade waste service income fell £70k short of target despite continuing to contribute to overheads
findings.detail: The trade waste service underperformed its income budget by £70k in 2025-26. Despite the service generating a positive contribution to council overheads, it is not reaching its income targets. This indicates the service is not delivering expected financial returns.
findings.matters: Trading service income shortfalls indicate portfolio management challenges; lenders monitor council trading performance as part of assessing financial resilience
findings.figures: £70k overspend due to shortfall in trade waste income compared to budget
findings.quote: £70k overspend due to a shortfall in trade waste income compared to budget. The service continues to generate a contribution to overall overheads but falls short of its overall income target.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Waste transport costs overspent £131k with reliance on hired vehicles pending new bin wagon delivery in 2026-27
findings.detail: The Customer and Digital directorate incurred £131k additional spend on waste services transport despite repairs being under budget. The council is dependent on external vehicle hire as a temporary solution. New bin wagons are expected in 2026-27 which should reduce this cost pressure, but until then the structural cost overspend will continue.
findings.matters: A known structural cost pressure consuming resources with only a one-year fix timeline makes this a material item for budget forecasting and for lenders assessing cost control
findings.figures: £131k net overspend on waste transport; delivery of new bin wagons anticipated 2026-27
findings.quote: £131k net overspend on waste services transport cost. Whilst the repair costs remain under budget, the external vehicle hire costs are substantial. The delivery of the new bin wagons is anticipated in 2026/27, and this will reduce the reliance on externally hired vehicles.

findings.paper_title: Capital and Balance Sheet Outturn 2025-26
findings.headline: Capital programme slipped £4.630m in final quarter, with waste fleet (£1.453m) dependent on August vehicle delivery and leisure works delayed by external contractors
findings.detail: Capital programme reduced from £19.993m (Q3) to £15.363m (Q4). Waste fleet represents the largest slippage at £1.453m, with council expecting five new vehicles in August. Leisure refurbishment (£1.042m) is delayed partly due to connection works 'outside of the Councils control'. Disabled facilities grants (£359k), Jubilee Gardens (£182k), and multiple other schemes show timing delays. The pattern suggests delivery and supply chain challenges across the programme.
findings.matters: A lender assessing the council's ability to execute planned investment needs to understand delivery risk. Multiple substantial slippages, especially on essential services like waste collection and schemes with external dependencies, indicate execution challenges that could affect service continuity or require rephasing.
findings.figures: £4.630m net variance Q3 to Q4, £1.453m waste fleet, £1.042m leisure refurbishment, £359k disabled facilities grants, £182k Jubilee Gardens
findings.quote: The total cost of the Council's capital investment programme for 2025/26 has decreased from £19.993m at Quarter 3 to £15.363m at Quarter 4.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B3 Financial Reserves Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Council earmarking £621k for restructuring and service reconfiguration to deliver savings
findings.detail: The council has reserved £621k to fund restructuring costs and service reconfiguration required to achieve budget savings. This indicates the council is expecting to need organisational changes to maintain financial balance.
findings.matters: Needing to reserve substantial funding for restructuring to deliver savings signals the council is planning cost reductions and service changes to balance the budget—indicating financial pressures beyond routine efficiency gains.
findings.quote: £621k is reserved to meet any restructure costs required to deliver savings or a reconfiguration of service delivery.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B3 Financial Reserves Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Council holding £2.977m business rates equalisation reserve following recent income reductions
findings.detail: The council has established a £2.977m reserve specifically to manage fluctuations in business rates income, acknowledging that some of this has already been drawn down during the current settlement due to recent reductions. The 2026/27 budget does not require use of this reserve, but future use remains under consideration.
findings.matters: A multi-million pound business rates equalisation reserve signals the council has experienced material income shocks in this volatile revenue source and is protecting against further reductions—a key concern for lenders assessing revenue stability.
findings.figures: £2.977m, with some already realised during current settlement
findings.quote: The council has set aside £2.977m to manage one-off reductions in business rates some of which has been realised across this settlement.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B1: Report of the Chief Finance Officer – robustness of the 2026/27 budget and the adequacy of financial reserves Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Government funding is expected to change during the multi-year settlement period despite January settlement
findings.detail: While a multi-year settlement was announced in February 2026, the CFO notes funding assumptions have been volatile and expects further changes to government funding figures during 2026/27-2028/29. Budget is based on February 2026 settlement figures.
findings.matters: Funding volatility could force mid-year budget revisions or trigger reserve draws if income falls short of assumptions; limits planning certainty for a multi-year forward plan
findings.figures: Final Local Government Finance Settlement published 9 February 2026, multi-year settlement
findings.quote: While this is a multi-year settlement there is a reasonable expectation that some government funding figures will change across the period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B1: Report of the Chief Finance Officer – robustness of the 2026/27 budget and the adequacy of financial reserves Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Council has committed to £37.714m capital programme over 2026-2029 with leisure, town centre and infrastructure investment
findings.detail: The capital programme includes ongoing leisure facility improvements, Leyland town deal delivery, play areas and open space upgrades, and waste fleet investment. Projects require business case approval before funding allocation.
findings.matters: Represents substantial financing commitments with ongoing revenue implications for interest, maintenance and asset management; material constraint on financial flexibility
findings.quote: The proposed Capital Programme for 2026 to 2029 of £37.714 million is included at Appendix F1 of the budget reports.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B1: Report of the Chief Finance Officer – robustness of the 2026/27 budget and the adequacy of financial reserves Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: General fund reserves will be held at minimum adequate level of £4m with no buffer above target
findings.detail: The council plans to maintain £4m in unallocated reserves, which it identifies as its minimum adequate level for managing short-term risks. This represents no headroom; any reserve draw would mean holding below minimum.
findings.matters: Thin reserves limit flexibility to absorb unexpected costs or revenue shortfalls; any adverse variance would force immediate corrective action, spending cuts, or reserve draws
findings.figures: £4m target, forecast to retain over £4.0m
findings.quote: The target level of general fund reserves is £4m over the medium term and importantly, the MTFS does not rely on utilising general fund balances to meet any deficits over the three-year period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B1: Report of the Chief Finance Officer – robustness of the 2026/27 budget and the adequacy of financial reserves Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Council closed a budget gap identified in February 2025 through increased income and cost reductions
findings.detail: The council had identified a budget shortfall in February 2025 but achieved balance for 2026/27 through a combination of increased income sources and delivered cost reductions across departments. This shows they faced financial pressure but were able to manage it.
findings.matters: Indicates the council had real budget stress but demonstrated management capability to address it; important signal for understanding what pressures they operate under
findings.figures: budget gap identified February 2025, now closed
findings.quote: Through a combination of increases in income and cost reductions that are contained within the proposals presented to Council, the forecast budget gap for 2026/27 presented to the Council back in February 2025 has now been closed.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget 2026/27 Medium Term Financial Strategy and Capital Programme 2026-2029 Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: New statutory food waste requirement initially unfunded (£945k pressure) but source of ultimate funding resolution unclear
findings.detail: Council identified £945k annual revenue pressure for mandatory food waste collections, which it had assumed would be funded via government New Burdens grants. No new funding was provided. The budget subsequently includes £1.3m capital investment for the service, but the method for resolving the recurring revenue pressure is not explicitly stated, suggesting the council had to find funding from constrained budgets.
findings.matters: Unfunded statutory mandates force reallocation of resources from other services; unclear resolution suggests budget flexibility is limited
findings.figures: £945k identified as unfunded pressure; £1.3m capital investment for implementing statutory weekly food waste collections
findings.quote: There appeared to be no new funding in respect of food waste revenue costs which the Council had assumed would be funded by New Burdens funding due to this being a new statutory requirement placed on the council. As such, a potential further pressure of £945k would be incorporated within the MTFS.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget 2026/27 Medium Term Financial Strategy and Capital Programme 2026-2029 Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Fit for the Future savings programme delivers only 65% of identified target in 2026/27, with remaining shortfall still being developed
findings.detail: Council identified £1.452m in potential savings but forecast only £941k actual delivery in 2026/27. A further £511k is identified for 2027/28, but nothing is confirmed for 2028/29 despite forecast deficits in that year. The council acknowledges 'work has begun on further options', indicating gaps remain unfilled.
findings.matters: Consistent shortfall in savings delivery suggests either targets are set optimistically or services are difficult to reform; accumulating gaps worsen the deficit position
findings.figures: £1.452m identified; £941k delivered 2026/27 (65% achievement); £511k planned 2027/28; unidentified balance for 2028/29
findings.quote: The programme is on track to save approximately £941k in 2026/27 with most elements either already in place or forecast to be in place by 1 April 2026. There is a further £511k identified for 2027/28 and work has begun on further options to be brought forward to address budget gaps

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget 2026/27 Medium Term Financial Strategy and Capital Programme 2026-2029 Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: 2026/27 balanced budget depends entirely on one-off £1.2m pension fund relief that will not recur
findings.detail: The Lancashire Pension Fund triannual revaluation produced an unprecedented reduction in employer contribution rates, falling from 18.3% to 8.7%. This generates a non-recurring saving of £1.2m. Without this windfall, the council would run a deficit in the first year of the MTFS, masking underlying structural pressures.
findings.matters: Balancing budgets with one-time windfalls rather than structural measures suggests the underlying financial position is weaker than the headline balance implies
findings.figures: Contribution rate reduction from 18.3% to 8.7%; estimated one-off saving £1.2m
findings.quote: The valuation has seen significant pension fund surpluses and as a result unprecedented reductions in employer pension contributions are proposed. Following the conclusion of the consultation the reduction for South Ribble Council is from 18.3% to 8.7% (9.6%). Estimated savings are from this are around £1.2m

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget 2026/27 Medium Term Financial Strategy and Capital Programme 2026-2029 Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Fair Funding 2.0 creates permanent funding loss of £500k in 2026/27 growing to £900k by 2027/28 despite transitional protection
findings.detail: The new government funding formula produces a 5% reduction in the council's funding baseline. Even with transitional protection factored in, the council faces structural income reductions that grow over the MTFS period. The council explicitly states this is a 'significant adverse impact' with funding assessment 'significantly lower than current funding levels'.
findings.matters: Structural cuts to government funding are not one-off events and cannot be addressed through temporary measures; they require permanent service reductions or tax rises
findings.figures: 5% reduction on 2025/26 baseline; losses approximately £500k (2026/27) rising to £900k (2027/28)
findings.quote: The Fair Funding 2.0 assessment has a significant adverse impact upon the Council still with the assessment of required resources being significantly lower than current funding levels. While transitional protection is incorporated into the figures it still means a reduction of 5% on 2025/26 funding levels.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget 2026/27 Medium Term Financial Strategy and Capital Programme 2026-2029 Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Forecast deficits of £1.774m in 2027/28 and £2.647m in 2028/29 remain unresolved with only exploratory 'options' identified
findings.detail: The council acknowledges large budget deficits in years 2 and 3 of the MTFS but has not developed firm savings plans to address them. The strategy states 'options that can be considered' and that 'work has begun on further options', indicating solutions are not yet determined. This leaves a significant structural gap between forecast spending and available funding.
findings.matters: Unresolved multi-year deficits signal potential future service cuts, borrowing, or reserve depletion; a lender would view this as latent financial stress that could crystallize within the loan term
findings.quote: The forecasted budget deficit in 2028/29 is estimated to be £2.647m and the MTFS sets out options that can be considered to bridge this gap

findings.paper_title: Appendix G Capital and Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Strategy
findings.headline: Waste fleet is ageing and requires £4.696m investment over four years
findings.detail: The council identifies that its waste fleet is ageing and is investing £4.696m on new vehicles between 2025/26 and 2028/29. This is a significant capital commitment for essential service delivery.
findings.matters: This is a large, necessary capital outlay for core services. Overruns or slippage would further pressure a council already forecasting budget gaps.
findings.quote: The waste fleet at South Ribble is ageing and the council is investing £4.696 million in new vehicles between 2025/26 and 2028/29.

findings.paper_title: Appendix G Capital and Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Strategy
findings.headline: Town Deal project expects to deliver net income stream to help manage future budget deficits
findings.detail: The council received £25m from a successful Town Deal grant and expects the regeneration project to deliver a 'net income stream to the council helping it to manage future budget deficits.' However, the document notes 'An assumption of some net income has been made but this will be updated as plans are finalised and is anticipated to increase.' This is speculative income baked into deficit projections.
findings.matters: Income projections from major regeneration projects often slip or disappoint. If the assumed income does not materialise, it would worsen the forecast deficit.
findings.figures: £25m Town Deal funding; net income amount assumed but unspecified
findings.quote: It is expected that this will also deliver a net income stream to the council helping it to manage future budget deficits. An assumption of some net income has been made but this will be updated as plans are finalised and is anticipated to increase.

findings.paper_title: Appendix G Capital and Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Strategy
findings.headline: 7% of the council's directorate budgets depend on rental income from 130+ commercial units, a dependency that will grow
findings.detail: The council states that approximately 7% of gross directorate budgets are funded by net income from investment in capital assets (over 130 units across multiple sites). The document notes this percentage 'will increase' as the council invests further in income-generating assets across the Medium-Term Financial Strategy period. This is a significant and growing operational dependency on asset performance.
findings.matters: Heavy reliance on asset rental income is a vulnerability if the property market weakens, tenants struggle, or vacancy rates rise. A lender will want to know this percentage and what happens to the budget if collections fall.
findings.figures: ~7% of directorate budgets; 130+ units across numerous sites
findings.quote: The council's gross directorate budgets are funded by approximately 7% through the income generated by these assets. As the council invests in income generating assets throughout the MTFS period the percentage identified above will increase.

findings.paper_title: Appendix G Capital and Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Strategy
findings.headline: The council has moved to forbid borrowing solely for yield generation
findings.detail: A capital programme objective now states 'Borrowing solely for the purpose of generating yield is no longer permissible.' This is a change in policy, indicating the council previously considered or pursued this strategy and is now constrained—a sign of tighter financial discipline or external pressure.
findings.matters: This rule change suggests either a prior incident of unproductive borrowing or new external constraints. It limits the council's flexibility to generate revenue through debt-funded investment.
findings.figures: None given
findings.quote: Borrowing solely for the purpose of generating yield is no longer permissible.

findings.paper_title: Appendix G Capital and Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Strategy
findings.headline: Council forecasts a budget gap in coming years and is preparing to use capital receipts for revenue spending
findings.detail: The council explicitly states it faces a 'forecast budget gap in the coming years' and is adopting a flexible use of capital receipts strategy to provide tools to manage this period. This is not hypothetical—it is framed as necessary preparation for expected deficits. The strategy allows capital receipts to fund transformation, redundancy costs, and service efficiency projects rather than only capital assets.
findings.matters: A lender assessing creditworthiness needs to know whether the council has a credible plan to close deficits. Using capital receipts for revenue spending is a one-off solution that creates future pressure if receipts dry up.
findings.figures: £2.647m in efficiency savings required by 2028/29; forecast budget gap (amount unspecified)
findings.quote: Given the forecast budget gap in the coming years and the prospect of Local Government Organisation the Council needs all the tools available to them that may be required in this period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix H1 Treasury Strategy
findings.headline: IFRS 16 leasing accounting standard may increase measured borrowing requirement and require raising of Operational Boundary
findings.detail: The new accounting standard for leases (IFRS 16) was implemented in 2024/25. The council states it 'may increase the CFR and hence there may be a need to raise the Operational Boundary' with a dedicated report to follow if this occurs.
findings.matters: Off-balance-sheet lease obligations becoming on-balance-sheet liabilities could increase the measured underlying borrowing need, signalling a larger structural financing requirement than currently visible
findings.figures: No impact figures provided; described as potential future outcome
findings.quote: New regulations on accounting for leases introduced by IFRS 16 may increase the CFR and hence there may be a need to raise the Operational Boundary. A dedicated report will be brought to Council if this is the case.

findings.paper_title: Appendix H1 Treasury Strategy
findings.headline: Council financing capital programme by depleting reserves rather than external borrowing, with projected reduction in investment balances
findings.detail: The council is maintaining an 'under-borrowed position' by using cash and reserves to fund capital expenditure instead of taking external loans. Section 37 states this strategy is driving 'projected reduction in investments.' The council intends to 'continue where possible' using internal borrowing to avoid interest costs on external debt.
findings.matters: Depletes financial buffers and indicates capital expenditure is being funded from cash reserves rather than from operational capacity or external financing, which reduces flexibility for future pressures
findings.figures: Projected reduction in investments shown in Table 6; specific amounts not detailed in narrative
findings.quote: The Council is currently maintaining an under-borrowed position. This means that the capital borrowing need (ie the Capital Financing Requirement) has not been fully funded with loan debt as cash supporting the Council's reserves, balances and cash flow has been used as a temporary measure. This strategy is prudent as interest payable on debt would be significant and will be continued where possible.

findings.paper_title: Appendix D: Cumulative Budget Deficit & Budget Strategy 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.headline: Trade waste income target not being achieved, with £68k shortfall budgeted as a cost pressure
findings.detail: The council explicitly acknowledges that trade waste ongoing income targets have not been met, listing this as a cost pressure rather than assuming achievement. This indicates either weaker commercial demand than budgeted or overly optimistic assumptions about the commercial market.
findings.matters: Unachieved commercial income targets signal either service demand problems or competitive weaknesses in council commercial operations
findings.figures: £68k shortfall in 2026/27
findings.quote: Trade Waste - ongoing income target not achieved 68

findings.paper_title: Appendix D: Cumulative Budget Deficit & Budget Strategy 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.headline: Revenue Support Grant is declining by 37% over the MTFS period, from £4.771m to £3.006m
findings.detail: The council's Fair Funding Assessment Revenue Support Grant falls from £4.771m in 2026/27 to £3.906m in 2027/28 and £3.006m in 2028/29. This £1.765m reduction (37%) represents structural loss of government funding that must be offset by service cuts, income generation, or reserves.
findings.matters: Declining grant funding reduces financial flexibility and forces difficult trade-offs between raising council tax, cutting services, or depleting reserves
findings.quote: Fair Funding Assessment - Revenue Support Grant (4,771) (3,906) (3,006)

findings.paper_title: Appendix D: Cumulative Budget Deficit & Budget Strategy 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.headline: Food waste service implementation will cost £945k in 2026/27 alone
findings.detail: The council faces a cost pressure of £945k for food waste staffing and other operating costs in 2026/27, representing one of the largest single budget pressures listed. This suggests either new statutory obligations or expanded service provision with substantial labour implications.
findings.matters: A single service line consuming nearly £1m indicates new regulatory requirements or service expansion that will absorb resources and limit flexibility elsewhere
findings.quote: Food Waste Staffing/Other operating cost 945

findings.paper_title: Appendix D: Cumulative Budget Deficit & Budget Strategy 2026/27 to 2028/29
findings.headline: South Ribble faces a cumulative budget deficit of £1.774m in 2027/28 rising to £2.647m in 2028/29
findings.detail: The council balances its budget in 2026/27 but then faces growing structural deficits. Expenditure is projected at £18.564m in 2027/28 against funding of £16.791m, and £19.274m against funding of £16.627m in 2028/29. The gap widens substantially in year three.
findings.matters: An unresolved structural deficit of this scale represents a material risk to financial sustainability and the council's creditworthiness
findings.quote: (Surplus) / Deficit - 1,774 2,647

findings.paper_title: Appendix B2 Risks to the Medium Term Financial Strategy Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Council is under-borrowed with significant gap between capital funding requirement and actual borrowing
findings.detail: The council has not borrowed to the full extent of its capital funding requirement, leaving a material gap. However, the council has capacity to borrow further whilst remaining within the Prudential Indicator framework if previously allocated funding sources fail to materialise.
findings.matters: Under-borrowing may indicate either prudent management or underutilised capital capacity; the identified gap affects future borrowing decisions and the pace at which capital schemes can be delivered.
findings.figures: not specified
findings.quote: The council is under-borrowed, i.e. it continues to have a significant gap between its capital funding requirement and the amount it has actually borrowed. As such, provision is available for the council to borrow whilst remaining within the Prudential Indicator framework, should funding sources previously allocated to projects no longer be available.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B2 Risks to the Medium Term Financial Strategy Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Council income streams from property rentals, planning, garden waste and car parking face downside risk outside its control
findings.detail: The council's major revenue streams include property and housing rentals, planning fees, garden waste subscriptions, and car parking charges. The paper identifies that reductions in these income sources, which lie outside council control, could leave services under-funded.
findings.matters: Commercial income streams are volatile and dependent on economic conditions; loss of this income would exacerbate the budget deficit without corresponding service cuts.
findings.figures: not specified
findings.quote: The major income streams that the council benefits from include property and housing rentals, planning, garden waste subscriptions and car parking. Reductions in income outside the control of the council could leave services under-funded.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B2 Risks to the Medium Term Financial Strategy Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation scheduled for 1 April 2028 falls within MTFS period but planning is not included
findings.detail: The current timetable for Lancashire's local government reorganisation would create new unitaries from 1 April 2028, falling within the 3-year MTFS period. However, the MTFS makes no provision for the impact or changes that reorganisation would bring, as the fundamental changes cannot be foreseen at this stage.
findings.matters: Organisational restructuring could disrupt budget delivery, alter income streams, require transitional funding, or create unforeseen liabilities; the lack of contingency planning is a material governance risk.
findings.figures: 1 April 2028
findings.quote: The current timetable for reorganisation across Lancashire would lead to new unitaries formed from 1 April 2028. The MTFS makes no provision for the impact or changes this would lead to but clearly this would be within the MTFS period.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B2 Risks to the Medium Term Financial Strategy Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Forecast cumulative budget deficits of £1.774m and £2.647m in 2027/28 and 2028/29 with savings plan still under development
findings.detail: The MTFS projects significant deficits in years 2 and 3 of the strategy period. The council has identified the need to develop a further savings programme and income generation opportunities to balance the budget, with monitoring overseen by Senior Management and Senior Leadership Teams. Minimum general fund balance of £4m has been set as a buffer for temporary financial pressures.
findings.matters: Growing deficits indicate the council may need to draw on reserves or implement deeper savings; lenders need confidence in the delivery of the identified savings programme.
findings.figures: £1.774m (2027/28), £2.647m (2028/29); minimum general fund balance £4m
findings.quote: The MTFS includes forecast cumulative gross budget deficits of £1.774m and £2.647m in 2027/28 and 2028/29 respectively. To balance the budget over the course of the MTFS we will need to further develop the savings programme, including opportunities for income generation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B2 Risks to the Medium Term Financial Strategy Accessiblereporttemplate SRBC
findings.headline: Business rates account for 40% of council income but face system uncertainty with rebasing and revaluation
findings.detail: The council faces significant risk from changes to the Business Rates Retention Scheme, including new multipliers, rebasing, and re-measurement still to be undertaken. Business Rate Pooling has been rendered effectively redundant by the reforms in 2026/27, removing a previously predictable funding mechanism. The council must make annual assumptions on write-offs, appeals, growth, and reliefs, which has become more complex.
findings.matters: A 40% income stream with heightened uncertainty directly affects the council's borrowing capacity and repayment ability, and the loss of pooling removes a mitigation strategy.
findings.figures: approximately 40% of the council's income
findings.quote: As Business Rates account for approximately 40% of the council's income, this is a significant risk

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Monitoring Report Q3
findings.headline: Interest receivable £300k below budget due to lower cash balances or interest rate decline
findings.detail: Corporate budget shows £300k underachievement in interest income (largest variance in that directorate). The council attributes this to interest rates and available cash balances being lower than anticipated. This is material as interest income reflects reserve position and short-term investment rates, suggesting either reduced cash liquidity or treasury forecasting shortfall.
findings.matters: Lower interest income may indicate smaller cash reserves than budgeted, reducing the council's financial flexibility and liquidity buffer.
findings.figures: £300k shortfall in interest receivable income
findings.quote: Interest receivable is under-achieved against the budget by £300k due to interest rates and cash balances available being lower than anticipated.

findings.paper_title: Revenue Budget Monitoring Report Q3
findings.headline: Property portfolio overspend £358k at Q3, growing from £237k at Q2, driven by rental income shortfall and maintenance surge
findings.detail: Property directorate forecast overspend increased from £237k in Month 6 to £358k by Q3. This includes £47k underachieved rental income from vacant investment property units and reduced income from Moss Side Community Centre during refurbishment, £81k utilities overspend (primarily surface water in car parks £22k and Civic Centre £33k), and £145k maintenance overspend. The council describes this maintenance as necessary work to 'ensure buildings are up to date with maintenance ahead of lease renewals'.
findings.matters: Investment portfolio performance and maintenance backlog are key indicators of asset quality and financial sustainability for lending decisions.
findings.figures: £358k overspend at Q3 (up from £237k at Q2), £47k rental shortfall, £145k maintenance overspend, £81k utilities increase
findings.quote: £145k overspend due to an overall increase in spend on repairs and maintenance, mainly within the Investment property portfolio, including some general repairs within the Community Centres and Civic Centre. This includes works to ensure buildings are up to date with maintenance ahead of lease renewals.

findings.paper_title: South Ribble Audit Findings Report 2024-25 For Committee
findings.headline: New property valuer engaged without signed terms of engagement and evidence gaps identified.
findings.detail: For 2024-25 revaluations covering £56.293m of land and buildings, council engaged new valuer but did not have signed terms of engagement in place before work started (contrary to best practice). Evidence to support valuer judgements was not always initially available, requiring additional audit procedures.
findings.matters: Absence of documented engagement terms and evidence gaps weakens control over a significant balance sheet estimate (property valuation) and indicates process gaps in managing expert services.
findings.figures: Land and buildings valuation £56.293m; investment properties reclassified £10.565m
findings.quote: As part of our audit work we identified that whilst the Council engaged the services of a new valuer for 2024/25, the Council did not have a signed terms of engagement. Best practice suggests signed terms of engagement should be in place before work is undertaken. Evidence to support valuer judgements was not always initially available, which resulted in the audit of revaluations taking longer than expected.

findings.paper_title: South Ribble Audit Findings Report 2024-25 For Committee
findings.headline: Multiple unresolved cybersecurity deficiencies with compliance deadline of March 2026.
findings.detail: Council is working toward MHCLG cyber assessment framework compliance with actions due March 2026. Currently lacks: formal supplier cybersecurity risk assessment process, formal vulnerability management process, user access reviews (none in last 12 months), privileged user activity reviews, and monitoring of scheduled IT system changes.
findings.matters: Unresolved cyber vulnerabilities expose the council to breach, operational disruption, reputational damage, and potential GDPR fines. 43% of UK organisations reported cyber attacks in the last 12 months.
findings.figures: 43% of organisations report having experienced a cyber breach or attack in the last 12 months (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, April 2025)
findings.quote: we note that the Council is working to achieve a cyber security policy that is fully compliant with MHCLG's cyber assessment framework (CAF). The Council has submitted its plan to MHCLG however, it still has a number of actions to complete, which it aims to achieve by March 2026. Full compliance should enable the Council to respond more effectively to security incidents, minimising potential damages and downtime. In addition, the Council has a cyber incident response plan and playbook, but these are in draft.
